title: Grid path planning (demo from a paper-style method)

paper.name: Illustrative path-planning paper (demo)
paper.one_line: Plan a collision-free path on a discrete grid from a start cell to a goal cell by expanding lowest-cost neighbors.

yes: 4-connected neighbor moves with uniform step cost
partial: Heuristic used for informed search (paper may name A*; we use Manhattan distance)
missing: Exact hardware timing and compute budget

supported_by_paper: Search expands cells by lowest path cost (open set / priority expansion).
Obstacles are treated as blocked cells the planner must not enter.
Success is a path from start to goal; failure is reported when no path exists.
assumptions: World is a fixed 20×14 grid (paper scale / map size not specified for this demo).
Moves are up/down/left/right only; diagonal moves are disabled.
Every free step costs 1; no terrain costs from the paper.
Heuristic is Manhattan distance — a common choice when the paper is ambiguous.
Obstacles are axis-aligned blocks the user can place; not scanned from a figure.

explain_templates.found: The planner found a path of {length} steps (cost {cost}). Cells were expanded in lowest-cost order; the heuristic biased expansion toward the goal. This matches the paper's discrete search framing; continuous vehicle motion is an assumption we did not simulate.
explain_templates.blocked: No path exists under the current obstacles and move rules. The open set emptied before the goal was reached — the same failure mode a grid planner reports when the free space is disconnected.
explain_templates.trivial: Start and goal are the same cell, so the path is empty. Change either position to see planning behavior.
